Voronoi Territory Tiles of the Cells in a Field

Source: R/figure-data-images.R
TerritoryTiles.Rd

Computes the Voronoi tessellation of the cells around a square field and caps every territory at cap from its cell by moving the polygon vertices that lie further away onto that radius; cells on the outer hull (unbounded territories) get a regular 12-gon of radius 0.7 * cap. Each tile carries a class from classes (first matching entry), and tiles are ordered for drawing by order (classes listed first are drawn first, all others afterwards; ties keep cell order). Requires 'deldir'.

Usage

TerritoryTiles(
  cells,
  centre = NULL,
  size,
  cap = 11,
  margin = 30,
  classes = list(),
  default = "other",
  order = c("other", "tumour"),
  centre_cell = NULL,
  id = "row",
  offset = NULL,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  label = "label"
)

Arguments

cells

Data frame of cells.

centre

c(x, y), a data frame with x, y, or NULL with centre_cell.

size

Field width.

cap

Maximum territory radius.

margin

Neighbourhood kept around the field for the tessellation.

classes

Named list: class name to labels; unmatched cells get default.

default

Class of unmatched cells.

order

Classes drawn first, in this order.

centre_cell, id, offset

As in CellMapData().

x, y, label

Column names.

Value

A list of class phenoscapR_territories with tiles (data frame with tile, x, y, class), centre, size and extent.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("deldir", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(2)
  d <- data.frame(x = runif(300, 0, 100), y = runif(300, 0, 100),
                  label = sample(c("t", "a"), 300, TRUE))
  tt <- TerritoryTiles(d, c(50, 50), 40, cap = 5, classes = list(tumour = "t"))
  head(tt$tiles)
}
#>   tile        x        y class
#> 1    1 43.95380 69.24557 other
#> 2    1 39.75610 68.45388 other
#> 3    1 38.17729 64.30769 other
#> 4    1 44.59806 64.97032 other
#> 5    2 48.07636 75.33569 other
#> 6    2 48.08042 76.69321 other
